list_entry.title: An issue in dispute between Yolanda

A.explanation: Since A doesn't discuss joyriding at all, we have no support that he disagrees with this part of Y's statements.

B.explanation: 2nd person doesn't actually talk about damage to property, just physical harm. But presumably he'd agree with this anyway.

C.explanation:
Neither person was assessing whether X was more / less / equally criminal to Y.

Person 1 was assessing whether X was more / less / equally dangerous to Y.

D.explanation:
This is not my favorite answer. Arjun isn't directly weighing in on the comparison question: Which is more dangerous -- joyriding or hacking?

Arjun just points out that hacking also has the potential to do physical harm.

But it's supportable that Arjun would say "hacking is basically as dangerous as joyriding", since he's enthusiastically! disagreeing with Yolanda, by bringing up that hacking can also do people physical harm.

Yolanda explicitly says "joyriding is the more dangerous crime (than hacking)".

E.explanation: For someone to disagree with this claim, they'd be arguing that "treating private property recklessly is never a dangerous crime". There's no way Person 1 or 2 is taking that side of the issue.
